doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

chapter: Georgette's memories of the Basie band
title: Band children and falling under the train
summary: Georgette remembers the band kids, Pepper and Judy, and slipping under a train, saved by Freddie Green.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: [inaudible] But I remember Sweets’ daughter, not Sweets, it was Snooky. He had three kids there was Pepper, Judy and there was another, we had a difference in age. And a lot of us, the parents would pack the lunches, and I remember we would wait, it was like after when they’d all settle down, we would go in and pull these boxes down and Pepper, Snooky’s son, would pull down the cake and the cake was all over him and then we would get in trouble. You know we were always, there were so many of us I can remember different members of the band the kids when we traveled. I remember once I pulled away from my mother and my father. And I was with —

Freddie Green and the trains would come in and they would stop, you know, abruptly back and forth, and between where you stepped from the curb to the train there was an opening, it wasn’t closed off. And I slipped under somehow. And I remember he just came, I don’t know where he was, but he came and pulled me up and I remember being very upset about it.
Yes, scared to death, me too.
And I threw up. But anyway I remember more than falling under the train was I had on this slip —

[inaudible] But you know somebody would always take her. So but the trouble is the train would be, you know how they’re [sounds like] yilking and shaking, and she just fell down under, and almost fell under.
